# Typography

Heading, Body, Metric and Code are the text styles for all work.

**Kind:** Foundation

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/styles/Typography.mdx`

## Overview

PLUS is all sans. Every heading, metric and body style is Google Sans Flex with rounded ends and automatic optical sizing, and Google Sans Code is for code. Large headings (32, 28 and 24) are regular (400); smaller headings and metrics are medium (500); body is regular. Each style carries its own letter spacing, tighter as the size grows and looser as it shrinks. Pick a style by its role on the page, never by how big it looks. Tutors and students read on laptops and desktops, so check each size on a desktop screen from 768 up.

```css
font: var(--heading-md);
letter-spacing: var(--heading-md-tracking);

font: var(--body-default);
letter-spacing: var(--body-default-tracking);

font: var(--metric-lg);
letter-spacing: var(--metric-lg-tracking);
font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums;
```

Figma holds `Heading/*`, `Body/*`, `Metric/*` and `Code/default`, bound to the typography variables (Tokens: Typography).

## Type scale

Every text style binds to a typography variable (family, weight, size, line height and letter spacing) and is sized in `rem` (1 rem = 16 px) so text scales with browser settings. Never type a raw size or detach a style.

### Body, metric and weights

- **Body/large (16/24):** long-form reading such as lessons, help articles and quotes (quotes use the body family; never add a decorative face).
- **Body/default (14/20):** default interface text and control labels (sets the 24, 32 and 40 control heights). Do not use heading styles inside components; use body with a heavier weight instead.
- **Body/small (12/16):** secondary meta text, tags, statuses, counts and tooltips.
- **Metric (large, medium, small):** featured numbers such as session counts or scores.
- **Paragraph spacing:** space blocks with Section and stack tokens (Spacing), never a paragraph-spacing style.

| Style | Size/line | Weight | Role | Sample |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Body/default/regular | 14/20 | 400 | Paragraphs and descriptions |  |
| Body/default/medium | 14/20 | 500 | Control labels and text beside an icon |  |
| Body/default/bold | 14/20 | 600 | Inline emphasis, used sparingly |  |

## In code

Set component text with `font: var(--heading-sm)` and `letter-spacing: var(--heading-sm-tracking)` (or the same pair for `--body-default`), and icon glyphs with `--icon-sm`, `--icon-md` or `--icon-lg` (Iconography). Never hardcode a font size, family or weight.

### Family, weight and tracking tokens

| Token | Value | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--type-family-heading` | Google Sans Flex | Headings and metrics |
| `--type-family-body` | Google Sans Flex | Body text |
| `--type-family-code` | Google Sans Code | Code |
| `--type-family-brand-heading` · `--type-family-brand-body` | Google Sans Flex | Marketing and docs heroes only, never the product |
| `--type-weight-regular` | 400 | Body text and headings xxl, xl and lg |
| `--type-weight-medium` | 500 | Headings md to xxs, metrics, labels and icon-paired text |
| `--type-weight-semibold` | 600 | Inline bold only: strong in running text, never a component or text style |
| `--type-tracking-tighter` · `-close` · `-tight` · `-snug` · `-none` · `-open` · `-loose` | −2% · −1.5% · −1% · −0.5% · 0 · +0.5% · +1% | The letter-spacing steps the companions below read |
| `--heading-xxl-tracking` · `--heading-xl-tracking` | −2% | Headings 32 and 28 |
| `--heading-lg-tracking` | −1.5% | Heading 24 |
| `--heading-md-tracking` | −0.5% | Heading 20 |
| `--heading-sm-tracking` · `--heading-xs-tracking` | 0 | Headings 16 and 14 |
| `--heading-xxs-tracking` | +1% | Heading 12 |
| `--body-lg-tracking` · `--body-default-tracking` · `--body-sm-tracking` | 0 · +0.5% · +1% | Body 16, 14 and 12 |
| `--metric-lg-tracking` · `--metric-md-tracking` · `--metric-sm-tracking` | −1% · −1% · 0 | Metrics 28, 24 and 16 |

### Text-style classes

Markup without its own stylesheet can use the generated utility classes (`.heading-xxl` to `.heading-xxs`, `.body-lg`, `.body-default`, `.body-sm`, `.metric-lg` to `.metric-sm`), which set `font` and `letter-spacing` together. The metric classes also set tabular figures. Component stylesheets use `font: var(--…)` directly, add `letter-spacing: var(--…-tracking)` beside it, and add `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` to a metric.

```jsx
<p className="body-default">Helper text</p>
<h2 className="heading-md">Section title</h2>
```

## Heading levels

Headings step down one size per nesting level; containers use a fixed title size. Reserve `Heading/xxlarge` (32) and `Heading/xlarge` (28) for heroes, empty states and metric-heavy dashboards, never a page title. Use a heading style rather than bold text or a size change, because heading styles carry the structure assistive technology reads.

| Level | Style |
| --- | --- |
| Page title | Heading/large · 24 · the page's one h1 |
| Section title | Heading/medium · 20 · h2 |
| Subsection title | Heading/small · 16 · h3 |
| Modal title | Heading/medium · 20 · the modal's h1, named by aria-labelledby |
| Card, popup and flag title | Heading/xsmall · 14 · one level below its section |
| Group label (menu group, table head) | Heading/xxsmall · 12 · a group or head cell, never a heading tag |

Every page has one `h1` (visually hidden when a tab strip replaces a visible page header). Card titles take the heading tag one level below their section.

## Labels

Button, tab and menu labels use `Body/default/medium` (`font: var(--body-default); letter-spacing: var(--body-default-tracking); font-weight: var(--type-weight-medium)`), which pairs with icon stroke weight. Never set regular or bold weight, or a heading style, on a button or tab label. A Sidebar tab is a navigation row: its label is regular weight at rest and medium when selected.

Do: Body/default/medium on a button or tab label.

Don't: Regular or bold weight, or a heading style, on a button or tab label.

## Code

`Code/default` (12/16, Google Sans Code) sets code samples, token names and property values. In CSS, `var(--code-default)` sets `0.875em` of the parent size so inline code scales with surrounding text.

## Truncate and wrap

Names and titles truncate; primary content wraps. Never shrink font size to fit a long string.

- **Titles and names** truncate to one line with an ellipsis; expose the full text on hover or in the detail view.
- **Descriptions** clamp at 3 lines unless configured to wrap.
- **Session notes and help answers** wrap in full. Table cells truncate by default and opt into wrap per column.

### Truncate a long name to one line

A student name in a roster row.

Do: One line with an ellipsis. The Status keeps its place.

Don't: The name wraps onto extra lines and makes the row taller than its neighbors.

## Do and don't

### Use a heading style

Introduce a section with a heading style, not with bold body text.

Do: Heading/small, tagged as the section's heading.

Don't: Bold body text looks like a heading but carries no structure.

### Do not skip heading levels

Headings step down one level at a time.

Do: h1, then h2, then h3.

Don't: An h3 straight after the h1 skips the h2.

## Headings, numbers and mono

### Headings

Headings are Google Sans Flex: 400 at 32, 28 and 24, then 500 from 20 down so they hold their place over body text. Size, line height and tracking step down together (sizes are in the type scale above, tracking in the tokens table, and the level for each role in Heading levels).

Text styles use only 400 and 500. Do not add a 600 or 700 weight to a heading.

### Numbers

Metric styles are Google Sans Flex 500 with tabular figures. Use the `.num` class, or `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`, for numbers that line up vertically: table columns, times in schedules and timelines, and counts in lists. Running text keeps proportional figures. A time or duration ("3:30 to 4:30", "12 min") takes the body or heading style of its context, never mono.

Do: Metric/large for the figure.

Don't: Heading/medium for a number.

### Mono

Google Sans Code is for code, token names, property values and machine IDs such as a session ID or a URL. Never use it for metrics, times or counts: mono digits are wide and read as a data dump. `Code/default` is 0.875em of its parent, and in a table it pairs with `Body/small`.

Do: Metric/large for the count, mono for the session ID.
Don't: Mono for the count.

## Accessibility

- Keep one `h1` per page and step down one heading level at a time (`h1` → `h2` → `h3`); the HTML tag sets the outline while the token sets the visual size.
- Pair text styles with `color/text/*` tokens to meet WCAG AA 4.5:1 contrast (Color).
- All type tokens use `rem` or `em` so text scales with browser zoom and font-size preferences.
